what: Unions, yellow vests protesters, and student protesters hold a fourth consecutive weekend of protests across France with about 146,000 participants. (AFP) (Al Jazeera)

Malaysia's Registrar of Societies deregisters the opposition coalition Perikatan Nasional, citing internal disputes and breaches of the constitution, preventing its component parties from contesting forthcoming elections under a common coalition banner. (Reuters)

U.S. news organizations project that the Democratic Party will control the House of Representatives and the Senate in the upcoming 120th Congress, ending the Republican Party's majority in both chambers. (Reuters) (The Guardian)

Spanish transport minister Óscar Puente resigns after the country experienced two train collision disasters in one year, the Adamuz derailment in January and the Toledo collision last week, which had a combined casualty toll of 115 deaths and 492 injuries. (CNN)

The Brazilian Superior Electoral Court fines Meta Platforms R$7.5 million (US$1.34 million) for failing to comply with judicial orders concerning the 2026 presidential election, while finding insufficient evidence of deliberate electoral interference. (AFP via Le Monde)

Thousands of students and teachers march through Athens, Thessaloniki, and Patras in Greece to protest against the rising cost of living, calling for affordable student housing and more state investment in education. (AP)
Rioters in Paris attack police with projectiles, but are dispersed with tear gas and water cannons. A gendarmerie helicopter is deployed to locate remaining rioters. (France 24)

The Federal High Court of Nigeria invalidates former vice president Atiku Abubakar's nomination as the African Democratic Congress candidate for the 2027 presidential election, ruling that the party's leadership was improperly constituted. (Reuters)
Protests are held across France for the third consecutive weekend. (AP) (France 24)
Protests and riots are held in Bilbao, Spain, after and during a political event hosted by far-right commentator Vito Quiles. At least nine people are arrested. (El Constitucional)
The Parliament of Romania appoints Luca Niculescu as the new Prime Minister, succeeding Ilie Bolojan who resigned amid a politicial crisis. (Reuters)
More than 200,000 people march in Amsterdam, Netherlands, to protest against Israel's genocide in Gaza and the Dutch government's support of the Israeli military. (Al Jazeera)

A small boat reportedly carrying about a hundred people, mostly migrants, capsizes off Yenne, Senegal. Sources report that four bodies have been recovered, while several others are still missing. Search operations are launched by authorities. (Al Jazeera) (BBC News)
The death toll from the boat capsizing yesterday off the coast of Kébémer, Louga, Senegal, increases to 39 people. (AFP via France 24)
Five people are killed while two others are injured in an explosion at a suspected illegal fireworks factory in Malasiqui, Pangasinan, Philippines. (The Philippine Star)
At least one person is killed and 527 others are injured as Typhoon Champi swept near Taiwan. (DW)
A Russian Air Force Antonov An-12 crashes near Kemerovo, Russia, killing all 19 people on board. (AP) (The Independent)
Twenty-four people are killed and 24 more are rescued after a ship carrying funeral goers capsizes in Bayelsa State, Nigeria. (Arab News)

At least 69 people are killed and 179 injured during a collision between two high speed trains carrying a total of 544 passengers between Los Yébenes and Urda, in the Province of Toledo, Spain. (Sky News)

A tanker and the cruise ship American Heritage collide in the Mississippi River of the United States. All passengers and crew aboard both ships survive, with 32 people hospitalized for injuries. (BBC News) (CNN)

A Mw 5.7 earthquake strikes central Japan with its epicenter in Shizuoka Prefecture, while also affecting Aichi, Gifu, Nagano and Yamanashi prefectures. At least 22 people are injured. (AP) (NHK World-Japan)
Twenty-four people are killed and 24 more are injured after a bus collides with a truck on a highway in Makueni County, Kenya. (AP)
Thirteen people are killed and 50 others are seriously injured in a multiple-vehicle collision involving 86 vehicles on the Trakia motorway near Yambol, Bulgaria. (Al Jazeera) (Plovdiv24)
A construction site is hit by a tornado in Kepez, Antalya, Turkey, killing four workers and injuring another. (AP)

The South Korean Fair Trade Commission issues fines of ₩331.1 billion (US$247 million) for Woowa Brothers and ₩300.8 billion ($222 million) for Coupang, finding that their food-delivery platforms restricted competition by requiring restaurants to match rival platforms' terms. (AFP via France 24)

Canada's federal government invests up to C$1.6 billion (US$1.1 billion) in Toronto-based artificial intelligence company Cohere, taking an equity stake as part of a C$7 billion (US$5 billion) funding round intended to expand domestic computing infrastructure and AI development. (AFP) (Reuters)

The United States announces the suspensions of Rwanda and South Africa from duty-free trade benefits under the African Growth and Opportunity Act beginning January 1, 2027, citing trade barriers, human rights concerns, and threats to U.S. interests. (Reuters)

Bangladeshi police and 42 platoons of the Border Guard Bangladesh deploy tear gas, stun grenades, batons, and surveillance drones against garment workers across Dhaka, Savar, Ashulia, Gazipur, and Narayanganj protesting for a minimum wage hike from ৳12,500 (US$100) to ৳30,000 ($240). Protesters bloc
The Central Bank of Paraguay reports providing partial refunds to 1,812,348 eligible Ueno Bank depositors following the bank's collapse. (France 24)

Villa Vie Residences suspends operations of the Odyssey in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, after running out of money amid sharply higher fuel costs, forcing 203 passengers to disembark with seven hours' notice. (AFP)

The Joint Organisations Data Initiative reports that Saudi Arabia's oil exports rose in September to their highest level since the outbreak of the war in February, despite Houthi attacks on Red Sea ports and infrastructure. (Al Jazeera)
Russian independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta announces plans to cease operations on 9 November, citing pressure from Russian authorities. (Reuters)
South Africa cuts fuel levies by R3.00 (US$0.18) per litre of diesel and R1.50 ($0.09) per litre of petrol from November 4 to December 1 after fuel prices reach record highs. (AFP)
Seychelles-based cryptocurrency exchange KuCoin ends services for customers in Russia and Belarus, citing ongoing sanctions. (The Crypto Times)
South Korea withdraws additional embassy staff from Ukraine following a dispute over two captured North Korean soldiers who were transferred to South Korea. (AFP via RFI)

Ireland's Dáil Éireann approves legislation removing the requirement for United Nations authorization before deploying more than 12 Defence Forces personnel overseas for peacekeeping missions, while retaining approval by the government and parliament. (France 24)
Libya's eastern-based House of Representatives approves a 2019 maritime boundary agreement with Turkey and repeals two 2020 decisions that rejected the accord. (Reuters)

Poland's ambassador to Romania, Paweł Soloch, and Poland's ambassador to China, Jakub Kumoch, resign from their positions in protest of the suspension of Polish Constitutional Tribunal president Bogdan Święczkowski. (24 Kanal) (Firstpost)
The United States Department of State designates three Guatemalan criminal groups as foreign terrorist organizations for providing material support to Mexican cartels. (AFP via Macau Business)

Russia bans two French lawmakers, Arthur Delaporte and Sacha Houlié, and two journalists, Ariane Chemin and Paul Gogo, from entering the country for allegedly harassing Xenia Fedorova, the head of RT France, from 2017 to 2023. (Al Jazeera)
Iran designates the Argentinian naval and air forces as terrorist organizations, in response to Argentina designating the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as such in March. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)
Qatar and Turkey sign a defense pact in Istanbul. (AFP via France 24)

The Kenyan health ministry reports that the country has discharged its last Ebola patient from a hospital in Nairobi after eleven contact cases were treated. Kenya will be declared Ebola-free on December 23 if no one else exhibits symptoms. (DW)
Eight more people in Bangladesh are reported to have died from dengue fever, bringing this year's outbreak's death toll to 499. (BSS)
Four more children in Bangladesh are reported to have died from measles, bringing the death toll to 1,299. (BSS)

The World Meteorological Organization reports that global concentrations of carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide reached record highs in 2025, with carbon dioxide averaging 426.8 parts per million. (AFP via France 24)

The United States Food and Drug Administration approves the first generic version of lenacapavir, a twice-yearly HIV prevention injection expected to cost about US$40 annually in 120 low- and middle-income countries. (AFP via France 24)
Eight more people are reported to have died from dengue fever in Bangladesh, bringing this year's outbreak's death toll to 491. (BSS)

The Nigerian health ministry expands contact tracing after confirming an imported Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja, identifying at least 44 contacts while investigating additional people who may have been exposed and strengthening infection-control measures. (AFP via RFI)
France reports the first human case of the livestock Shamonda virus in a patient who died after being hospitalized with an unrelated condition. (Reuters)
Teghaza 001, a Martian meteorite discovered in 2022 in the Sahara in Mali, is reported to be 4.1 billion years old. (Reuters)

The Italian Data Protection Authority fines American technology company Meta €805 million (US$887 million) after it was found that the Facebook app on Android had access to users' photos and videos without specific consent or disclosure. (BBC News) (Reuters)

Cybersecurity firm CloudSek reports that the Kazakhstan-linked hacker group Silent Lynx used an autonomous agent to breach Tajikistan's government database and steal more than 2,000 national security-related documents. (The Record) (Reuters)

American technology company Apple experiences an outage with several of its services, including Apple Pay, iCloud, the App Store, and AppleCare. The company's spokesperson attributed the problems to an internal update and rules out a cyberattack. (Time)
American video game publisher Electronic Arts, which was recently bought-out by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, announces the closing of its Canadian studio BioWare. (Kotaku)

Indian certificate authority eMudhra has its private keys compromised, revealing that some of them were extremely insecure single digit numerals. Major web browser developers Mozilla, Google, and Apple subsequently block the certificates. (The Register)
